title: 2022 surplus allocation and e-scooter bylaw
subtitle: Year-end capital report, Maltby Road wildlife crossing, reserves and debt statement, and a staff report on personal e-scooters.
overview: The committee reviewed the city's 2022 year-end financial results and recommended how to allocate the $13,698,567 operating surplus. Most of it would go to reserves, including capital and infrastructure funds, police-related reserves requested by the Police Board, and utility reserves for water, wastewater and stormwater. {{vote:m1}} Staff stressed that surplus funds are one-time money and do not solve future tax pressures, and that every dollar placed in reserves reduces what must be raised later through taxes and rates.

The committee also recommended funding adjustments in the capital report, including $375,000 for a permanent wildlife crossing and fencing on Maltby Road. {{vote:m2}} It received the long-term statement on reserves and debt for information. {{vote:m3}}

In the public services portion, the committee recommended that staff bring a report and draft bylaw on personal e-scooters to the July 5, 2023 meeting. The normal public pre-consultation will be skipped because of time and the provincial pilot ending in January 2025. {{vote:m6}} Council would hear public feedback through delegations in July. Guelph Police Services is asked to provide input on enforcement, crash-data reporting and public education. All these items go to Council for final decision.

decisions.detail: The committee recommended allocating the 2022 operating surplus among capital, contingency, police, utility and other reserves and reserve funds {{vote:m1}}.

decisions.item: Capital budget adjustments and Maltby Road wildlife crossing
decisions.detail: The committee recommended approving the funding adjustments in the capital monitoring report and $375,000 from the Infrastructure Renewal Reserve Fund for a wildlife crossing and fencing on Maltby Road {{vote:m2}}.

decisions.item: Long-term financial statement: reserves and debt
decisions.detail: The committee received the 2022 reserves and debt statement for information {{vote:m3}}.
The committee amended the motion so that only public pre-consultation on developing the bylaw is skipped, leaving room for later consultation {{vote:m5}}.

The committee recommended that staff bring a draft bylaw or Traffic Bylaw amendment permitting personal e-scooters to the July 5, 2023 meeting, with police input on enforcement, crash reporting and education {{vote:m6}}.

debate: Staff described the surplus as one-time money. One councillor asked that the public not conclude it removes future tax pressure. Staff said it is too early to say, and that the earlier forecast for 2024 to 2027 was in the 6% range.

Councillors questioned adding to water, wastewater and stormwater reserves that are near target. Staff said the long-term capital needs are large and the targets are under review. One councillor worried it would be hard to draw the money back out later.
Staff said the Police Board's request includes a one-time pilot of two officers dedicated to the downtown, with more information to come to Council later in May.

On e-scooters, a delegate from a local active transportation group supported the motion, citing last-mile trips and lower costs. Councillors raised concerns about riders on sidewalks and multi-use paths, children's safety and helmets.

Staff said there is no time for normal public consultation and limited staff capacity to run or report on a scooter program. Staff expected only a narrow bylaw, and the mover said a long engagement process would not suit a pilot ending in 2025.
